annotation.title_clean: Regulation of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) in Artworks by Robots and Algorithms
annotation.title_en: Regulation of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) in Artworks by Robots and Algorithms
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Raevita, F.; Uzma, N.L.S.; Alfarizy, M.
annotation.summary_en: Indonesian normative-juridical article on who owns copyright in artworks produced by robots and AI algorithms, and how moral and commercial rights of creators are protected. It argues that only humans hold copyright and that broader, adaptive legal reform is needed to fit AI creativity.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots and algorithms lack consciousness and legal identity, so they cannot own copyright.
Programmers, users, or both may claim copyright depending on their creative contribution.
Some jurisdictions treat fully AI-generated works as public domain.
Current copyright laws do not fit AI-generated works, so broader and more flexible reform is needed.
Reform needs stakeholder consultation and international cooperation.
